ai.description: The Indian Tent Turtle grows to 26 cm. It features a high, tent-shaped carapace with a distinct vertebral keel and a greyish-brown shell. The head has a red or yellow spot behind the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Tent Turtle is best identified by its distinctively high, roof-like carapace featuring a prominent, continuous black or dark brown vertebral keel.
ai.habitat: The Indian Tent Turtle inhabits slow-moving rivers and streams with abundant aquatic vegetation, typically found at low-to-moderate altitudes across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Indian Tent Turtle is primarily diurnal, often basking on logs or rocks during the day to regulate its body temperature before foraging for aquatic vegetation and insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Indian Tent Turtle is oviparous, laying 3–14 elliptical eggs in a single clutch. Breeding occurs from October to March, with nesting typically peaking in winter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Tent Turtle occurs across northern, central, and eastern India, primarily within the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Mahanadi river systems at low elevations.
